paper.title: Fighting Bandits with a New Kind of Smoothness

unmapped: Losses (negative gains) in [-1,0]^N; 'loss-only' sign assumption is used critically in the analysis
Paper's N is the number of arms (canonical K)
settings.definition_quote: On each round $t = 1,\ldots, T$, a learner must choose a distribution $p_t \in \D_N$ over the set of $N$ available actions. The adversary (Nature) chooses a loss vector $\xx_t \in [-1,0]^N$. The learner plays action $i_t$ sampled according to $p_t$ and suffers the loss $\xx_{t,{i_t}}$. The learner observes only a single coordinate $\xx_{t,{i_t}}$

algorithms.name: GBPA with stochastic smoothing / bandit FTPL (with Geometric Resampling)

source.label: thm:tsallis
source.quote: Let $\tf(\XX) = \max_{p \in \D_N}\{\langle p, \XX \rangle - \eta S_\alpha(p) \}$. Then the GBPA$(\tf)$ has regret at most \EE\Regret \leq \eta \frac{N^{1 - \alpha} - 1}{1-\alpha} + \frac{N^\alpha T}{2 \eta \alpha}.

results.notes: Holds for any eta; horizon dependence only when eta tuned. Marked known since T appears in bound with fixed eta.

bound.regime: a_ts in (0,1), eta = sqrt(T(1-a_ts)/(2 a_ts)) N^{a_ts - 1/2}

source.quote: For any $\alpha \in (0,1)$, if we choose $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{T(1-\alpha)}{2\alpha}} N^{\alpha-\frac{1}{2}}$ then we have \EE\Regret \leq \sqrt{\frac{2 T N}{\alpha(1-\alpha) }}.

results.notes: eta depends on T, so known horizon.

source.quote: In particular, the choice of $\alpha = \frac 1 2$ gives a regret of no more than $2\sqrt{2 T N}$, recovering \citep[Theorem~5.7]{bubeck2012regret}.

results.notes: Paper notes it recovers a known bound; recorded as part of the corollary.

symbols.EmaxZ: expected maximum of N iid draws from perturbation distribution D
symbols.h_sup: supremum of the hazard rate of D

extra_assumptions: D continuous with support unbounded towards +infinity
exact gradient (expectation) used for estimation; FTPL with Geometric Resampling adds NT/(eM)

source.quote: The regret of the GBPA with $\tf(\XX) = \EE_{Z_1, \ldots, Z_n \sim D} \max_{i} \{\XX_{i} +  \eta Z_{i}\}$ is at most: \eta \EE[\max_{i} Z_{i}] + \frac{N(\sup h_\mathcal{D})}{\eta}T

results.notes: Theorem numbering inferred. Bound is for GBPA with exact sampling probabilities.

bound.regime: distributions in Table 1 with given parameters; Geometric Resampling with M = sqrt(NT)

extra_assumptions: perturbation distribution from Table 1 (Gumbel, Frechet, Weibull, Pareto, Gamma) with suitable parameters

source.quote: Follow the Perturbed Leader Algorithm with distributions in Table \ref{tab:distributions} (restricted to a certain range of parameters),  combined with Geometric Resampling (Section \ref{sec:ftpl:ftpl}) with $M = \sqrt{NT}$,	 has an expected regret of order $O(\sqrt{TN \log N})$.

results.notes: Corollary says M = sqrt(NT) while the text says M = NT suffices; GR bias term NT/(eM) with M=sqrt(NT) gives sqrt(NT)/e, still consistent. Compute: paper says sampling can be done efficiently.
